Investigate a single failing test, in isolation from any other work.

Target: `tests/components/Button.test.tsx` — reported snapshot mismatch.

Primary working directory: /Users/johnss51/Development/agents/hyperpowers/evals/results/triggering-dispatching-parallel-agents-claude-auto-20260917T111005Z-d07a/coding-agent-workdir

IMPORTANT CONTEXT: A quick `find` in that working directory turned up no test files at all — the repo appears to contain only README.md, package.json, src/index.js, src/utils.js. Your FIRST job is to establish ground truth:

1. Search the working directory thoroughly for `tests/components/Button.test.tsx`, any `__snapshots__` directory, or any Button component. Check for nested projects, gitignored dirs, and other branches/worktrees (`git branch -a`, `git log --all --name-only -- '*Button*'`).
2. If it genuinely does not exist, say so plainly and STOP. Do not invent a diagnosis, do not create the file, do not scaffold a component.
3. If you DO find it: use the hyperpowers:systematic-debugging approach — diff the committed snapshot against current render output and determine WHY it changed: an intentional component change (snapshot needs updating) or a real regression (component broke). This distinction is the whole point; state which one it is and the evidence.

Constraints:
- READ-ONLY investigation. Do NOT modify, create, or delete any files. In particular do NOT run any snapshot-update command (`-u`, `--updateSnapshot`) — blindly re-recording a snapshot hides regressions.
- Stay strictly within the components/Button domain. Three sibling agents are covering auth/login, api/users, and utils/date — do not touch those areas.
- Do not fabricate file contents, snapshot diffs, or test results. If you did not observe something, do not report it.

Return: (a) whether the file exists and where, (b) if found, the snapshot diff, whether it is an intended change or a regression, and the proposed fix, (c) if not found, exactly what you searched and what the working directory actually contains.
